A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a novel technique for clock recovery from data, based on a phase-only filter (POF) and have demonstrated that the POF can be implemented using a simple linear optical network.
we have demonstrated a new technique that allows for the recovery of a high-quality clock signal from RZ OON data with a record low power consumption.

we have demonstrated a novel technique for ultrafast optical clock recovery, which is based on phase-only optical filtering and which significantly improves the quality of the recovered clock compared to the use on a conventional Fabry-Perrot filter.
The main takeaway from our work is that

a phase-only filter can be used for ultrafast all-optical sampling, with a sampling time of 10 ps, and that the filter can be realized using a combination of a phase modulator, a dispersive delay line and a nonlinear optical loop mirror (NOLM).
the clock quality can be improved by more than 20 dB and the clock energy can be reduced by 3 dB by using a linear optical filter with a phase-only response instead of a Fabry-Pérot filter.
phase-only filters are capable of performing clock recovery from data with a bit rate as high as 160 Gb/s, with an energy efficiency of 0.1 pJ/bit.
